To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have found that loss of distinct chromsomal regions is associated with TP53 LOH in Li Fraumeni syndrome fibrosarcomas and that these regions contain genes involved in cell senescence and cell cycle control.

Loss of distinct chromosomal segments, including regions containing genes involved cell cycle control or tumour suppression, occurs at low cumulative PD in Li-Fraumani syndrome fibroblastic strains that show loss of heterozygozity for TP53.

loss of distinct chromosomic regions, associated with TP53 LOH, is detected in Li-Fraumi fibroblasts during in vitro passaging, and that the alterations detected in these regions are not associated with genetic instability or with somatic TP53 mutation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of genomic instability associated with loss of TP53 heterozygosity in Li-Fraumanis syndrome fibroblastic cell strains.
the identification of the genetic alterations that occur in Li-Fraumenti syndrome cell strains.
the genomic instability associated with LOH for the tumour suppressor gene TP53, which is the gene mutated in the majority of human cancers

the genomic changes detected in LF fibroblasts are associated with LOH for TP533.
genomic alterations associated with LOH for TP533 occur in Li-Fraumenti fibroblasts but are not detected in fibroblasts without TP53 LOH.
genomic instability, in terms of LOH for TP533 and CGH changes, is not a common event in LF cell strains, but that it may occur in some strains.

LOH in Li- Fraumeni fibroblasts is associated with genomic changes, which may include loss of chromosomal segments containing tumour suppressor or senescence genes, and may be a prelude to genomic instability and aneuploidization.
